messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

Text: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or plan to become pregnant. Having hypothyroidism during pregnancy may increase the risk of miscarriage, high blood pressure in pregnancy, pre-eclampsia, stillbirth, or premature birth, and untreated hypothyroidism can affect the baby's brain development. The benefit of treating hypothyroidism outweighs these risks, and levothyroxine should not be stopped during pregnancy.
Your dose needs are often higher during pregnancy. Your doctor will check your thyroid blood tests as soon as your pregnancy is confirmed and at least once in each trimester, and will usually put you back on your pre-pregnancy dose straight after you give birth, with another blood test 4 to 8 weeks later.
Tell your doctor if you are breastfeeding. Levothyroxine passes into breast milk, but no harmful effects on breastfed babies have been reported. Treating hypothyroidism properly may also help milk supply if it is low. Your dose needs may be different while you are nursing.

Choose a relation whose meaning and subject/object direction match the triplet even if the wording differs; choose 'None of the above' only if no candidate fits.
